title: A Protocol for FRET-Based Live-Cell Imaging in Microglia
protocol: Cultivate cells in an imaging-compatible dish.
Aspirate the medium from the flask.
Add 3 mL PBS (Ca2+/Mg2+ free) to the flask and gently swirl it.
Aspirate the PBS from the flask.
Add 500 μL trypsin 0.5% to the flask.
Tilt the flask up and down and from side to side for coverage.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 5 min.
Add 5 mL supplemented medium to the flask using a serological pipette.
Gently pipette up and down along the flask surface to collect detached cells.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 400 × g at 22°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the cells in 1 mL supplemented medium.
Count the cells in suspension using a cell counter or Neubauer chamber.
Add 2 mL supplemented medium to the imaging dish.
Add 2.5×104 cells to this dish.
Using a 1 mL micropipette, gently aspirate up and down the cell suspension in the dish, taking care not to introduce bubbles.
Incubate the cells 12–16 hours at 37°C (5% CO2) to allow attachment and spreading.
Transfect cells with a plasmid encoding a FRET probe and incubate for 16–20 hours to allow proper biosensor expression.
Prepare a 1.5 mL tube containing 200 μL JetPrime buffer for every imaging dish containing cells to be transfected.
Pipette 900 ng plasmid DNA into the tube.
Briefly vortex the mixture.
Add 1.8 μL JetPrime transfection reagent to the tube containing buffer and DNA.
Vortex the mixture immediately for 10 seconds.
Incubate the mixture at 22°C–25°C for 10 minutes.
Aspirate the medium from the imaging dish containing the seeded cells.
Add 2 mL of fresh supplemented medium to the dish.
Use a micropipette to add, dropwise, the entire volume of the plasmid-containing particles to the dish.
Incubate cells at 37°C (5% CO2) for 4 hours.
Aspirate the medium from the imaging dish after 4 hours.
Add 2 mL fresh supplemented medium to the dish.
Incubate the cells at 37°C (5% CO2) for 16–20 hours.
Bring cultures to a laminar flow hood.
Remove the medium from the imaging dish.
Add 2 mL saline (PBS or HBSS) gently.
Repeat adding and aspirating saline at least two times.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed imaging solution.
Incubate cells with imaging solution for 5–10 min at 22°C–25°C.
Return the cultures to an incubator depending on the application.
Supplement the media for long-term storage to avoid starvation/acidification of the culture.
Take the culture dish to the microscope for imaging.
Turn on the temperature controller and CO2/O2 regulators before incubating cells with imaging solution (at least 30 minutes in advance).
Choose the desired microscope objective and bring cells into focus.
Activate the mark-and-find option using the GFP filter to select cells with high expression of FRET probe.
Mark the desired positions by adding them one by one.
Set up software imaging parameters, exposure time, filter combination, and binning adjustment (if applicable).
Set up the focus and time-lapse routine for image acquisition.
Set exposure in the LAS AF software between 50-200 ms to achieve pixel intensity values of at least 800 and a maximum of 25000.
Set the DONOR channel light path for CFP excitation and collect CFP fluorescence.
Set the ACCEPTOR (FRET) channel light path for CFP excitation and collect YFP fluorescence.
Set the focus mode to adaptive mode.
Set the time interval between image sequences and recording interval in the time-lapse routine.
Perform a baseline recording of 5-10 minutes before adding any stimulus for internal control.
After baseline recording, pause the acquisition and apply the solution containing the stimulus.
Ensure exposure time is the same for DONOR and FRET channels.
Use adaptive focus built into the Leica FRET system or similar routines for long-term recordings.
Perform experiments at 32°C–35°C for consistent results.
Do not use light source at 100% power during acquisition.
Do not set exposure times higher than 300 ms.
Consider using binning to improve signal-to-noise ratio if necessary.
Open microscope data using FIJI software.
Subtract the image background.
Adjust brightness and contrast for the mask.
Threshold the images.
Generate the binary mask.
Mask DONOR and FRET channels.
Produce the ratio image.
Convert the image to 16-bit scale.
Apply a multicolor LUT.
Set up quantification parameters.
Quantify ROIs using the ROI manager.
Subtract background from DONOR and FRET channels separately.
Draw an ROI in a cell-free zone.
Measure the fluorescence of the ROI.
Subtract the measured values from each corresponding channel.
Adjust brightness and contrast for the images.
Save DONOR and FRET images as .tiff files.
Duplicate the entire FRET channel stack.
Threshold the desired ROI in the duplicated FRET channel stack.
Convert the thresholded ROI into a binary image.
Save the binary stack as .tiff and rename it to "mask."
Generate masked 32-bit float images of DONOR and FRET channels.
Rename the masked images to "masked DONOR" and "masked FRET."
Save the masked image stacks as .tiff files.
Generate a ratio image:
Go to Process -> Image calculator.
Choose image 1 (masked FRET).
Choose image 2 (masked DONOR).
Set operation to divide.
Check create new window and 32-bit float options.
Convert ratio image to 16-bit:
Go to Image -> Type.
Select 16-bit option.
Rename the image to “FRET-DONOR”.
Save as .tiff file.
Apply a gradient LUT.
Adjust image contrast.
Draw ROIs in cells or structures to be quantified.
Transpose ROI coordinate vectors to the ROI manager using the shortcut "t".
Set measurements to be extracted from ratio images:
Go to Analyze -> Set measurements.
Extract quantitative measures using the multiple measure function of the ROI manager.
Experimenter may save ROI locations for future reference.
Copy and paste values to a spreadsheet or Save as .csv for further quantitative analyses and statistics.
Display representative time series as intensity-modulated display (IMD) images:
Find the IMD FRET plugin at https://doi.org/10.17632/y6z2zmsx4f.1.
Download "IMDFret.txt" file.
In FIJI go to Plugins -> Macros -> Install.
Open DONOR, FRET and intensity-modulated (IM - duplication of the brightest channel) images.
Run IMDFret plugin.
Select numerator, denominator, and IM image.
Adjust the max/min ratio using multiples of 2.
Adjust the max/min intensity.
In the generated color-coded IMD stack, red-yellow represents high FRET, and blue-green represents low FRET.
Re-adjust brightness and contrast using sliders if necessary.
Do not skip step 16.
Alternatively, perform background subtraction using an average value with an in-built FIJI routine.
Go to Process -> Subtract background -> try different values of Rolling ball radius.
If subcellular structures are moving, register the FRET and DONOR channels before generating the ratio image.
Go to Plugins -> Registration -> Register Virtual Stack Slices.
